column4: First depositor inflates the share price and steals the next deposit
column5: First depositor inflates the share price and steals the next deposit -- ### Summary `Strategy.sol` mints shares from the raw asset balance with no virtual offset, so a first depositor who seeds one wei and then donates assets directly to the contract makes the next honest deposit round down to zero shares. ### Root Cause The share math reads the live balance instead of a tracked total, and nothing seeds the pool at construction.

column4: Depositing after an unreported loss steals value from existing holders
column5: Depositing after an unreported loss steals value from existing holders -- ### Summary While a position carries an unreported loss, `Strategy.sol` still prices new shares off the stale reported total, so a depositor entering just before the loss is booked buys in at a discount paid for by existing holders. ### Root Cause The reported total is refreshed on a harvest schedule rather than at deposit time.

column4: Activity window misconfiguration lets a stale pool pass the liveness check
column5: Activity window misconfiguration lets a stale pool pass the liveness check -- ### Summary `Leverager.sol:checkPoolActivity()` compares the last trade timestamp against an owner-set window with no upper bound, so a window set long enough makes a pool with no recent trades still read as active and borrowing continues against a stale price. ### Root Cause The configured window is never validated.

column4: Tick-range arithmetic overflows a uint16 and bricks every new position
column5: Tick-range arithmetic overflows a uint16 and bricks every new position -- ### Summary The tick-range width is stored in a `uint16` while the spacing multiplication that produces it is computed in a wider type, so a wide range wraps to a small value and every subsequent position is opened against a corrupted range, reverting all new deposits permanently. ### Root Cause An unchecked narrowing cast on the range width.
